query: Who has written more than 300 papers, Semyon Aranovich Gershgorin or Pavel Alexandrov?

retrieved_context: Semyon Aranovich Gershgorin: Semyon Aronovich Gershgorin (August 24, 1901 – May 30, 1933) was a Soviet (born in Pruzhany, Belarus, Russian Empire) mathematician.  He began as a student at the Petrograd Technological Institute in 1923, became a Professor in 1930, and was given an appointment at the Leningrad Mechanical Engineering Institute in the same year.  His contributions include the Gershgorin circle theorem.

Pavel Alexandrov: Pavel Sergeyevich Alexandrov (Russian: Па́вел Серге́евич Алекса́ндров ), sometimes romanized Paul Alexandroff or Aleksandrov (7 May 1896 – 16 November 1982), was a Soviet mathematician.  He wrote about three hundred papers, making important contributions to set theory and topology.
Semyon Aranovich: Semyon Davidovich Aranovich (Ukrainian: Семён Аранович, 23 July 1934, Derazhnya, Ukraine, Soviet Union – 8 September 1996, Hamburg, Germany) was a Soviet and Russian film director.
pipeline_result.rewritten_query: Papers by Pavel Alexandrov and Semyon Aranovich Gershgorin have been published in multiple prestigious journals.
